text:
anya: quick note — spotted reproducible kv-anchor drift on canary when onboarding redwood-magnet-13b-q2_k2 for long-context summarization. appears with interleaved prefill streams and tokenizer-v2 seam shifts.
devon: repro steps?
anya: two clients, staggered prefill windows, overlapping by 512 tokens, streaming to ~9k tokens. command:
```
python tools/repro_interleave.py --model magnet-13b-q2_k2 --clients 2 --prefills 8192,7168 --overlap 512 --max-tokens 9000
```
hugo: logs?
anya: pasted trimmed server output:
```
[2026-05-28T03:40:19Z] client=A PREFILL done base=0 len=8192 kv_slot=8192 fp=0x54af
[2026-05-28T03:40:20Z] client=B PREFILL done base=6656 len=7168 kv_slot=6649 fp=0x54ac
[2026-05-28T03:40:20Z] WARN kv_slot_mismatch expected=8192 got=6649
[2026-05-28T03:40:20Z] ERROR rope_phase_alias token_pos=7421 phase_delta=4
```
priya: single-client passes; multi-client fails ~1/60 runs. disabling rotary (`runtime::rotary_disable=true`) removes the observed semantic drift.
devon: that points to rotation math + quant combo. did you try serialized prefill?
anya: `runtime::prefill_serialized=true` also removes the flake. so concurrency window required.
hugo: two hypotheses: (A) allocator/remap race yields non-monotonic indices (B) quantized rotary accumulation amplifies tiny index skew into phase aliasing. both consistent with logs.
priya: can you attach per-layer rotary residuals and kv fingerprints to trace? /staging/traces/1772468019/ would be ideal. also include tokenizer boundary crc.
anya: pushed trace + micro repro harness to /staging/traces/1772468019/ and kicked off job repro-bisect-1772468019 on canary-3.
sre-bot: @anya job repro-bisect-1772468019 started on canary-3 :white_check_mark:
devon: next actions: 1) anya run single-threaded interleaved client to reproduce without allocator races 2) hugo run high-precision numeric diff of rotary kernel (q2_k2 vs float32) for layers 8-14 3) priya add a tiny guard in token remap that asserts monotonicity and logs the offending pair.
hugo: initial numeric probe shows layer10 residual ~3.1e-6 vs float32; small but multiplicative across layers. switching multiply accumulator to int32 in the quant kernel reduced residual by ~2.5x in a harness.
priya: good lead. but we need to avoid global locks. propose: add per-slot CAS for allocator and a runtime fallback flag `runtime::rotary_fallback_on_phase` that recomputes affected layers in float when phase_delta>1. cheap to implement and safe while we finish allocator fix.
devon: agree. also add a flaky CI test `eng-ml/longprefill_interleave` that runs the repro 300x to catch regressions.
anya: I'll open a tiny PR with failing test + trace first, then follow-up with CAS allocator patch and optional rotary-fallback. will tag @eng-runtime and @product if we need to gate rollout on Dedicated.
sre-bot: ticket created ML-ONBOARD-2781 (priority=P2) for follow-up :white_check_mark:
priya: one more: record a metric `rotary.remap_mismatch_rate` and an automatic canary hold threshold (e.g., >0.5% over 1h) so we can detect regressions early.
hugo: ack. I'll produce the numeric diff and a short patch that swaps accumulator type for q2_k2 rotary multiply as an experiment.
devon: thanks — this looks actionable. keep updates here and paste deterministic single-threaded repro when available. :mag:
